q: מה הקשר בין ALZHEIMER DISEASE (AD) לדיכאון?
o: רוב חולי ה- AD סובלים גם מדיכאון
דיכאון בחולי AD מתבטא פחות בהפרעות שינה ותיאבון
סימן מוקדם לדיכאון בחולי AD יכול להיות עליה באיריטביליות
סימן מוקדם לדיכאון בחולי AD הינו מחשבות אובדניות
explanation:
Depression can accompany Alzheimer disease and may first be noticed as a change in behavior. Families may describe new irritability, withdrawal, or disrupted appetite and sleep before the person reports sadness.

**Increased irritability can be an early sign of depression.** Ask when it started and whether it accompanies other mood symptoms.

**A. Most people with AD have depression.** Depressive symptoms affect more than 30% of people with AD. That estimate does not support assuming a majority.
**B. Fewer sleep and appetite changes.** Changes in both sleep and appetite are among the early manifestations to ask about.
**C. Increased irritability.** A new tendency to become frustrated or angry can prompt assessment for depression.
**D. Suicidal thoughts as the early sign.** Suicidal thoughts warrant immediate assessment when present. Irritability is the characteristic early clue among these choices.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 901.

q: An older patient with foot drop is beginning neuromuscular electrical stimulation. Why should the therapist provide rest intervals?
o: Stimulation mainly recruits slow units that recover only during sleep
Electrical recruitment of fatigable motor units can exhaust the muscle
Each stimulus transiently blocks transmission at the motor end plate
Repeated stimulation permanently reduces voluntary motor-unit recruitment
explanation:
**A.** Electrical stimulation recruits larger, fatigable motor units first. Rest between contractions reduces fatigue during the session.
**B.** Electrical stimulation can recruit large, rapidly fatigable units early. Rest between contraction sets limits fatigue and preserves the intended movement.
**C.** NMES triggers contraction and does not rely on temporary neuromuscular block.
**D.** Pacing the contractions addresses reversible fatigue, not permanent loss of voluntary recruitment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 826.

q: A 73-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment takes diphenhydramine nightly for sleep and reports feeling foggy the next day. Which approach to the drug is supported by Hazzard?
o: Increase the dose to overcome tolerance to its sedating effect
Avoid the drug as a primary treatment for insomnia
Continue the drug to improve cognition on the following day
Give the drug earlier in the evening to prevent next-day effects
explanation:
Diphenhydramine blocks central histamine receptors and also has anticholinergic effects. **Avoid it as primary insomnia treatment** when an older patient with cognitive impairment reports next-day fogginess.

**A. Increase the dose** Tolerance can develop rapidly, and dose escalation exposes the patient to more adverse effects.
**B. Avoid as primary treatment** Sedation can persist and cognition can worsen, while continued hypnotic benefit is limited.
**C. Continue to improve cognition** Delirium and decreased cognition are recognized adverse effects.
**D. Give earlier to prevent residual effects** Moving the dose earlier does not eliminate its long half-life or anticholinergic burden.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 661.

. Avoid as primary treatment** Sedation can persist and cognition can worsen, while continued hypnotic benefit is limited.
. Continue to improve cognition** Delirium and decreased cognition are recognized adverse effects.
. Give earlier to prevent residual effects** Moving the dose earlier does not eliminate its long half-life or anticholinergic burden.

explanationParts.text: Diphenhydramine blocks central histamine receptors and also has anticholinergic effects. **Avoid it as primary insomnia treatment** when an older patient with cognitive impairment reports next-day fogginess.

q: An 86-year-old man with severe COPD, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease has recurrent falls, difficulty preparing meals, and missed medications. Which assessment addresses the combined physical, functional, psychological, and social dimensions of his care?
o: Review glucose records and diabetes medication doses.
Measure spirometry and observe inhaler technique.
Perform an interdisciplinary comprehensive geriatric assessment.
Estimate filtration and review renal drug dosing.
explanation:
Multimorbidity can impair daily life in ways that no single organ review captures. **Interdisciplinary comprehensive geriatric assessment evaluates medical, functional, psychological and social needs together.**

**A. Review glucose records and diabetes medication doses** — Glucose results and drug doses matter but leave meal preparation, medication management and falls largely unexplored.
**B. Measure spirometry and observe inhaler technique** — Spirometry and inhaler technique address COPD. They do not show which daily tasks require help.
**C. Perform an interdisciplinary comprehensive geriatric assessment** — The team can relate falls and missed medicines to strength, cognition, treatment burden and support at home.
**D. Estimate filtration and review renal drug dosing** — Renal dosing can prevent harm but cannot, by itself, explain how he will obtain meals or take medicines safely.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 128–129, Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

optionRationales.body: . Review glucose records and diabetes medication doses** — Glucose results and drug doses matter but leave meal preparation, medication management and falls largely unexplored.
. Measure spirometry and observe inhaler technique** — Spirometry and inhaler technique address COPD. They do not show which daily tasks require help.
. Perform an interdisciplinary comprehensive geriatric assessment** — The team can relate falls and missed medicines to strength, cognition, treatment burden and support at home.
. Estimate filtration and review renal drug dosing** — Renal dosing can prevent harm but cannot, by itself, explain how he will obtain meals or take medicines safely.

q: An 83-year-old man with severe COPD, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure develops delirium while hospitalized with pneumonia. He was continent and cognitively intact at baseline. A Foley catheter was inserted on admission, but reassessment finds no continuing indication. Which device-related step fits delirium care?
o: Keep the catheter and treat bladder discomfort pharmacologically.
Remove the catheter and monitor voiding.
Continue catheter drainage until the infection resolves.
Limit mobility to prevent traction on the catheter.
explanation:
An indwelling urinary catheter is a modifiable delirium precipitant and a tether to the bed. Reassess its indication independently of the pneumonia.
**Remove the unnecessary catheter and monitor voiding.**

**A. Keep the catheter and treat bladder discomfort pharmacologically** — A sedating bladder drug adds a possible medication contributor without resolving the tether.
**B. Remove the catheter and monitor voiding** — Monitoring after removal permits prompt recognition of new urinary retention.
**C. Continue catheter drainage until the infection resolves** — Waiting for pneumonia to resolve prolongs avoidable immobility.
**D. Limit mobility to prevent traction on the catheter** — Restricting mobility adds another risk factor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 888, Tables 58-1 and 58-5

. Remove the catheter and monitor voiding** — Monitoring after removal permits prompt recognition of new urinary retention.
. Continue catheter drainage until the infection resolves** — Waiting for pneumonia to resolve prolongs avoidable immobility.
. Limit mobility to prevent traction on the catheter** — Restricting mobility adds another risk factor.

q: בת 92 סובלת מדמנציה בחומרה קלה, דיכאון ויתר לחץ דם. בתקופה האחרונה היא מרגישה כאב בטן תחתונה פתאומי, לחץ ללכת לשירותים, אך היא לא מצליחה להתאפק. לכן יש לה דליפות שתן בכמות קטנה בדרך לשירותים. איזו תרופה עלולה לגרום לתופעה זו?
o: DONEPEZIL (MEMORIT)
VALSARTAN (VECTOR)
AMIODARONE (PROCOR)
BISOPROLOL (CARDILOC)
explanation:
Cholinergic activity can increase urinary frequency and urgency. **Donepezil can precipitate urgency leakage by increasing acetylcholine availability.**

**A. Donepezil** — Acetylcholinesterase inhibition can accentuate bladder contraction and urgency.
**B. Valsartan** — Valsartan blocks angiotensin receptors and lacks this cholinergic mechanism.
**C. Amiodarone** — Amiodarone acts primarily on cardiac electrophysiology and is not a cholinesterase inhibitor.
**D. Bisoprolol** — Bisoprolol predominantly blocks cardiac beta-1 receptors and does not increase acetylcholine.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 703, Table 47-4.

q: Which definition of urinary incontinence is used in the chapter?
o: An urgent desire to void without any urine loss
A complaint of any involuntary urinary leakage
Voluntary voiding more than eight times each day
Involuntary urine loss exclusively during sleep
explanation:
Urinary incontinence is defined by a complaint of involuntary leakage. Urgency or frequency can occur without leakage, and nocturnal leakage is only one presentation.

**A. An urgent desire to void without any urine loss.** Urgency can occur while the patient remains continent.
**B. A complaint of any involuntary urinary leakage.** Any involuntary leakage meets the definition, regardless of frequency or volume.
**C. Voluntary voiding more than eight times each day.** Frequent voluntary voiding alone does not establish urinary leakage.
**D. Involuntary urine loss exclusively during sleep.** Leakage during sleep is one presentation. The definition also covers daytime leakage.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 699.

. A complaint of any involuntary urinary leakage.** Any involuntary leakage meets the definition, regardless of frequency or volume.
. Voluntary voiding more than eight times each day.** Frequent voluntary voiding alone does not establish urinary leakage.
. Involuntary urine loss exclusively during sleep.** Leakage during sleep is one presentation. The definition also covers daytime leakage.

q: מה מהבאים מהווה גורם סיכון להיפוגליקמיה בקשישים?
o: ירידה בראיה
טיפול ב- QUETIAPINE
טיפול ב- HYDROCHLOROTHIAZIDE
תסמונת קושינג
keySource: IMA 2023-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q134
explanation:
Hypoglycemia risk depends partly on whether the patient can select the correct dose, measure glucose and respond promptly. Sensory impairment may compromise each of those tasks.

**Poor vision is a practical risk factor for hypoglycemia.** The patient may misread the meter, choose the wrong pen or fail to dial the prescribed dose.

**A. Impaired vision.** Vision and hearing impairment join limited dexterity and mobility among practical barriers to safe self-management.
**B. Quetiapine.** Sedation may interfere with function, but quetiapine itself is not the sensory risk factor tested here. Hyperglycemia is a recognized metabolic concern.
**C. Hydrochlorothiazide.** A thiazide can worsen glucose tolerance and does not directly stimulate insulin release.
**D. Cushing syndrome.** Excess cortisol promotes insulin resistance and tends to raise glucose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p1584, Table 99-15.
